challenge.better_approach: Considered a tooth that only reports the duplicates: that leaves 0.6's rule broken on disk. Considered renumbering in the outline: the duplicates are all resolved records, so their numbers are cited nowhere live, and the fix belongs in the records and the reader, not the outline.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the duplicates are migrated rulings and spawned follow-ups quoting a parent's number, not two real questions given one number. The build measures each before changing any.
challenge.prior_art: 741d532640ac (PROVED today) built next_qnum and number_open, which this reuses; b3472c7ee794 placed the existing numbers by hand; f04df01693e2 made the joined proof hold over an empty corpus. None checks uniqueness.
challenge.real_collision: Outline 0.6 is Akien's line; bumping its number is measurement-settled (as 741d did), but rewording it to point at the mint changes his prose. That choice is carried as a hypothesis: bump unless the build measures that a bump cannot stay true.

answers.falsifier: a proof reds while any Q# is carried by two records, any outline marker has no record, or 0.6's stated next is below outline_check.next_qnum; it greens over the live corpus after the build
answers.from_idea: none, because it was measured, not imagined: joined.qnum over every record under CairnCommons/questions/ read 47 numbers on more than one record (240 records), and Q#126/Q#127 on none, in the house at ec53dff12 (2026-11-24)
answers.how: Measure why each duplicate reads its number (most open with 'Q#n (' or quote a parent's 'where Q#n stands open'); give each its own number or stop qnum reading a quoted parent's number; mint records for Q#126 and Q#127; and make outline 0.6 state the next number so it cannot fall behind next_qnum (bump, or point it at the mint). A new proof in outline_check holds all three over the live corpus.
answers.traces_to: Law 9 (outline 0.6: 'Its #n is its own and never changes' is broken on disk, and a broken spec line is red until fixed) and Law 1 (a Q# is the address a settled answer is found by; two records at one address re-derive which is meant)
answers.what: Every Q# names exactly one question record: no number is read off two records, every [Q#n] marker in the outline has a record carrying n, and outline 0.6 never states a next unused number below the one outline_check mints.

bullets.text: 47 Q# numbers are each read off more than one question record (240 records, all resolved); Q#126 and Q#127 stand in the outline with no record; 0.6 says 128 is next while records reach 135
